extended_notes: Archetypal low-mass SF cloud and the benchmark for CO-to-H2 work. M~1.5e4 Msun (Lada+2010: 14964 Msun); extinction-based d=153+/-8 pc (Lombardi+2010), Gaia/Zucker+2019 splits it into subclouds 130-160 pc. No OB stars; ~350 YSOs. Contains B18 B213 L1495 L1521 HL Tau. Strong 12CO self-absorption; 12CO traces the diffuse envelope while 13CO/C18O trace the filaments.

M~1.8e4 Msun (Lada+2010: 18438 Msun). Distance debated: 240+/-13 pc (Lombardi+2010 extinction) vs 294-320 pc (Zucker+2018/2019 Gaia); the cloud is inclined so NGC1333 (~293 pc) is nearer than IC348 (~321 pc). Two active clusters NGC1333 and IC348 plus B1 B5 L1448 L1455. Fully mapped in 12CO/13CO by COMPLETE.

Discovered as a distinct entity by Lada+2009. Nearly identical mass and size to Orion A (M~1e5 Msun; Lada+2010: 99930 Msun) but ~15-20x lower SFR - the key counterexample for SF-threshold arguments. d=450+/-23 pc (Lombardi+2010), 470 pc (Zucker+2019). Illuminates NGC1499. Low dense-gas fraction.

Northeastern continuation of the California cloud; often treated as one 'Auriga-California' filament ~80 pc long. Quiescent, low-column, few YSOs. Sits along the Radcliffe Wave. Boundary with California is arbitrary in CO.

Small high-latitude complex studied together with Ursa Major and Polaris Flare for cirrus IR/mass-surface-density properties. Translucent, essentially no star formation. d~213 pc (Zucker+2019/2020) puts it among the nearest CO-emitting clouds. Named as a distinct feature in Dame+2001.

Total mass ~5500 Msun, d~350 pc (co-distant with Ursa Major and the Cepheus Flare at ~370 pc). The reference non-star-forming/'quiescent' cloud - no protostars at all, so it is the standard control field for turbulence, filament, and Delta-variance studies (Herschel Gould Belt Survey MC1 field). Low CO excitation; large 12CO/13CO ratio.

One of the four main high-latitude cloud aggregations in the northern Galactic hemisphere (with Polaris Flare, Draco, and L134), per the Magnani+1996 northern high-latitude CO survey. Diffuse/translucent, Av~1, patchy weak 12CO with little 13CO. No star formation.

An intermediate-velocity cloud (v_LSR ~ -20 km/s) that nonetheless emits in 12CO - evidence of molecule formation in infalling/shocked gas. Distance is poorly constrained (few hundred pc to ~1 kpc); the 600 pc here is nominal only. Cometary morphology from ram pressure against the Galactic halo. Not star-forming.

GMC complex ~100 pc above the plane; ~2e5 Msun of HI, molecular skeleton at 337-370 pc (median 345 pc). Contains L1251 L1228 L1177 L1157 (the L1157 outflow is the canonical chemically active protostellar shock). Modest low-mass SF surveyed by Spitzer Gould Belt II. Distances span 300-450 pc across subclouds.

Background component of the Cepheus complex, associated with Cep OB3 at 600-800 pc. Contains the Cep OB3b cluster - a rare nearby example of an OB association actively disrupting its natal cloud. The full Cepheus complex (270-1000 pc) totals ~7.2e5 Msun, the most massive GMC in the Zucker+2022 3D sample.

Edge-on photodissociation region on the L1204 cloud, ionized by HD 211880 in Cep OB2. The standard PDR benchmark for 12CO high-J line ratios and [CII] modelling. Contains the S140 IRS1-3 embedded massive protostars.
Named local feature in Dame+2001, comprising the LDN 1200-series dark clouds. Low-mass, quiescent, with only scattered YSOs. Sits below the plane on the near side of the Local Arm.

Diffuse high-latitude complex, one of the nearest CO-detected structures (~230 pc). Weak, clumpy 12CO with essentially no 13CO; a target for CO-dark gas and low-Av CO-formation studies rather than star formation.

Large HII region ionized by HD 206267, surrounded by a ring of bright-rimmed globules (IC 1396A the 'Elephant Trunk') - the textbook radiative-driven-implosion / triggered-SF laboratory. Distance quoted between ~740 pc (2400 ly) and ~950 pc; ~900 pc adopted here.

The Cocoon Nebula plus a ~10 pc eastern 'streamer' of filaments. Herschel filament-width studies (0.1 pc characteristic width) were first made here. Distance historically 460-1200 pc; ~800 pc is the common modern value. Moderate low-mass SF.

Extensive foreground molecular sheet at ~600-800 pc that produces the Great Rift in the optical Milky Way and heavily confuses velocity-based distances toward Cygnus X behind it. Massive in total but low column density; scattered low-mass SF. A major source of extinction in this longitude range.

W80 complex: the North America (NGC 7000) and Pelican (IC 5070) nebulae are one HII region split by the LDN 935 dust lane. Ionizing source is the obscured O star 2MASS J20555125+4352246. Gaia distance ~795 pc. Active intermediate-mass SF along the interface.

Reflection nebula on the L1174 cloud illuminated by HD 200775. The single most-studied PDR after the Orion Bar - the reference object for PAH emission, H2 fluorescence, and CO rotational-ladder PDR models. Small mass; one Herbig Be star.

Local diffuse rift named in Dame+2001, the continuation of the Aquila/Cygnus rift system toward lower longitude. Low column density, weak 12CO, negligible star formation; mainly relevant as foreground confusion for inner-Galaxy sightlines.

Small, nearby (~227 pc), low-mass cloud named as a distinct feature in Dame+2001 and given a Gaia distance by Zucker+2019/2020. Translucent, no significant star formation. Useful as a clean low-column CO test case.

One of the nearest and best-studied translucent MBM clouds (d~100 pc, M~20 Msun). No star formation; used as a laboratory for CO chemistry and turbulence at Av<1 and for CO-dark H2 calibration. Weak, narrow 12CO lines.

Largest local complex by sky area; dominates the northern Galactic-plane extinction. Western portion spans l=25-33, b=1-6 and contains Serpens Main, Serpens South, W40 and MWC 297. Nearest layers ~270 pc; the complex is a distance-superposition (Zucker+2019 finds components from ~250 to ~600 pc), so 12CO velocity structure is heavily blended.

VLBA parallaxes give 436+/-9 pc for both Serpens Main and Serpens South (Ortiz-Leon+2017), settling a long-standing 260 vs 415 pc dispute. The W40 GMC alone is ~1.4e5 Msun. Serpens South is one of the densest known protocluster filaments; Herschel/Aquila was the flagship Gould Belt Survey field.

High-latitude streamers (L204, L169, and neighbours) extending north from the main Ophiuchus cloud, part of the Sco-Cen shell. Among the nearest CO gas (~130 pc). Translucent and largely starless; often used for CO-dark gas and dust-to-gas calibration.

Compact, isolated, cometary cloud at ~150-160 pc - one of the three nearest active SF regions. Head is the R CrA cluster (Coronet); a long low-density tail extends toward the Galactic plane. Small total mass (~1e3-1e4 Msun) but high SF efficiency in the head.

One of the four main northern high-latitude aggregations (Magnani+1996). d~110 pc. L183 is the classic prestellar core for depletion/deuteration chemistry (CO freeze-out, N2D+/N2H+); L134N (L183) is a standard astrochemistry template source. No protostars.

~1e4 Msun at ~145 pc, but almost entirely starless apart from B59 - the standard example of a cloud in a pre-star-formation state. Its ~130 dense cores define the observed core mass function that most closely resembles the stellar IMF (Alves+2007). Strongly magnetically aligned striations.

L1688 (rho Oph) is the densest nearby protocluster; L1689 L1709 L1712 form the eastern streamers. VLBA/Gaia distance ~138-147 pc. Compressed by the Sco-Cen OB association / Upper Sco winds, which drives its high SF efficiency (~1e4 Msun cloud, hundreds of YSOs). Very high extinction core (Av>50).

Six subclouds (Lupus I-VI) at 150-200 pc, with Lupus I-IV nearest (~150-160 pc). Low-mass SF only; Lupus III hosts the richest cluster. Lupus I shows a striking magnetically-regulated filament. Prime ALMA protoplanetary-disk survey target because of its youth and proximity.

Cha I (~190 pc) is actively forming low-mass stars; Cha II is less active; Cha III is essentially starless - a useful evolutionary sequence at fixed distance. Total complex mass ~1e4 Msun. Far from the plane and isolated, so foreground/background CO confusion is minimal.

The archetypal isolated filament: ~6 pc long, near-perfect cylinder, remarkably close to the critical line mass, with well-ordered striations feeding it perpendicular to the magnetic field. The standard test case for filament formation and accretion models. Almost no star formation (one candidate protostar).

The most prominent naked-eye dark nebula. d~180-200 pc, M~3500 Msun. Essentially starless despite high extinction - a key counterexample to simple density thresholds for SF. NANTEN 13CO/C18O mapping resolves it into ~10 quiescent cores with low turbulence.

Named local feature in Dame+2001 at ~700 pc. Modest mass with a few embedded low-mass sources; sits in a crowded southern sightline where 12CO velocity crowding from the Scutum-Centaurus arm complicates separation.

Four clouds A-D (Murphy & May): A, C and D at 700+/-200 pc, but cloud B is a background object at ~2 kpc and should be excluded from local-cloud samples. Individual clouds are 1e5-1e6 Msun in 12CO. Vela C is the most massive C18O cloud (~4.4e4 Msun) and hosts RCW 36. The nearest site of ongoing intermediate/high-mass star formation.

Embedded cluster in the Vela C ridge at ~900 pc; the nearest high-mass-cluster-forming clump. NANTEN2/Mopra 12CO show two colliding velocity components, making it a leading cloud-cloud-collision candidate (Sano+2018). Bipolar nebula morphology from a filament-perpendicular outflow of ionized gas.

~35 deg diameter evolved HII region/supershell at ~450 pc containing dozens of cometary globules (CG 1-30) whose tails point away from the Vela pulsar / zeta Pup. Foreground to the Vela Molecular Ridge on the sky - the two are frequently confused but are separable in velocity. CO is confined to the globules and shell walls.

GMC associated with the CMa OB1 association and Sh2-296, ~1.1 kpc. Long-argued supernova-triggered SF site (the Sh2-296 arc is likely an old SNR shell). Contains several embedded clusters and the CMa R1 reflection nebulae.

Subtends ~15.3 deg2 (~3000 pc2) with M~0.75e5 Msun. Distance ~830-900 pc, notably farther than Orion A/B though nearby on the sky. Contains a well-known ultracompact HII region and one of the most luminous and massive CO outflows known. Reflection-nebula association R2 gives it its name.

The best-studied GMC: M~6.8e4 Msun (Lada+2010: 67714 Msun), d=371+/-10 pc (extinction) to ~400-430 pc (VLBA/Gaia; the cloud is inclined with the ONC nearest at ~390 pc). Contains OMC-1/M42/Trapezium, OMC-2/3, the Orion Bar (the benchmark edge-on PDR), and the L1641 tail. CARMA-NRO Orion gives 12CO at ~8 arcsec.

Reflection nebula on the far western wall of the Orion-Eridanus superbubble, illuminated by Rigel. Distance quoted ~200-300 pc, well in front of Orion A/B. Very low column density with weak, patchy 12CO; a few T Tauri stars. Good test case for CO emission at low Av in an irradiated shell.

L1630: M~7.2e4 Msun (Lada+2010: 71828 Msun), d=398+/-12 pc, comparable in mass to Orion A but forming stars ~3x less efficiently. Contains NGC 2024 (Flame), NGC 2023, the Horsehead (B33), and NGC 2068/2071. The IRAM ORION-B large program is the reference wide-field multi-line dataset for CO isotopologue chemistry vs UV field.

MBM 20 region. One of only two high-latitude (|b|>30) clouds with confirmed star formation, at just ~140 pc - which makes it the standard example that SF is possible in a small, low-mass, translucent cloud. Herschel-resolved cores; total mass only tens of Msun.

Ionized rim of the Orion-Eridanus superbubble blown by successive generations of Orion OB1 stars. Associated swept-up molecular gas appears as diffuse, low-brightness 12CO east of Orion A/B. Important for large-scale feedback and for separating swept-up shell CO from the parent GMCs.

Western end of the Mon OB1 complex, containing the NGC 2170/2245/2247 reflection nebulae. Roughly co-distant with NGC 2264 (~720-800 pc). Modest mass; low-to-intermediate mass SF plus PDR interfaces well suited to CO excitation studies.

Gaia DR2 distance 723 (+56/-49) pc. Cloud mass ~2.8e4 Msun with ~3000 Msun around each of the two main clusters. Contains the Cone Nebula, the Christmas Tree cluster, and IRAS 12 S1. Site of an unbiased 12CO(1-0) outflow survey that found nine outflows; a benchmark for clustered low/intermediate-mass SF and mass segregation.

Ring of molecular clouds (B30, B35, and others) around the Collinder 69 / lambda Ori cluster (stellar mass 650+/-120 Msun, radius ~3 deg or ~20 pc) at ~400 pc. Widely interpreted as a supernova-cleared cavity: the ring is the swept-up remnant of the original cloud, so it is the cleanest nearby case of a CO shell being dispersed by feedback.

Long claimed as the nearest molecular cloud (early estimates 60-90 pc); modern work puts it at ~275-325 pc. The other high-latitude cloud with confirmed star formation (a small T Tauri association). Low mass (~30-200 Msun) with detectable 13CO and CS in its densest clumps - unusual for an MBM cloud.
